get.description: The zones analysed, and the box around them all. Other endpoints take one's key as `zone`.
Whether AIS is being recorded, and a count of what was seen lately.
Satellite passes over the zone (or all of them) since AIS was recorded there, latest first.
A frame's radar image at 20 m, cut into 256 px web map tiles; empty (204) where it has none.
A frame's radar backscatter (VV), to lay on the map at the coordinates in the pass detail.

The latest radar image of every place in the zone over the last `days`: newest pass on top. Empty (204)
where no pass imaged it.

Sentinel-2 true colour around a radar detection, the clearest within 3 days of it (none: null).
The first request looks it up (a few seconds); then it is kept.
AIS events going on during the last `hours`, latest first.
Last position of every vessel heard in the area in the last `minutes`.
Vessels by name (contains) or MMSI (starts with).
Your watch list, newest first, with the vessels heard that each entry matches.

post.description: Watch a vessel: an alert whenever it is heard on the coast, once per visit.

get.description: What is left to review across passes: candidates and reception gaps without a verdict, latest first.

put.description: Your verdict on a detection: a vessel with or without AIS, a reception gap, or not a vessel.

post.description: Sign in: a session cookie for this browser, valid 30 days.

get.description: Who is signed in on this browser, if anyone.

A company behind vessels (an OpenSanctions entity id): what the sources say it owns and manages,
and which of those vessels Uatu has heard.
The span of the AIS record.
Every AIS report in the area from `start` for `hours`, by vessel, to play back.
Where traffic gathers: vessel-hours per ~2 km cell over the last `days`.
The reports written so far (weekly, or by uatu-report), newest first.
AIS reception quality by ~2 km cell over the last `days`.
Land outlines over the whole coast (built once at startup from the zones' land masks).
Where the browser gets the optical imagery shown on land, under the radar.
The sea in view outside a pass's radar image (or all of it): to mark what that pass did not look at.
